newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Samgro suspends share trade from Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Samgro suspends share trade from Thursday.

text.p: Samgro Investment Holdings Ltd chairman Christo Wiese announced in a statement that trade in Samgro equity instruments would be suspended from Thursday as a result of the recent NBS-Boland link.
The suspension was neccessary in terms of a Johannesburg Stock Exchange rule requiring a listed pyramid company to hold at least 50 percent of the shares of a subsidiary.
"Samgro was the holding company of Boland Bank Holdings with an equity stake of 66.5 percent," the statement said.

"Flowing from the acquisition by NBS Holdings of the banking and financial services interests of Boland Bank Holdings in exchange for shares, the business of the latter will be wound up in the next few days and its shares distributed to shareolders."
Samgro will hold 14.9 percent of the merged operations of NBS and Boland and could expand that to almost 35 percent through the exercise of its option on a further 23 million shares.

Thursday's statement followed a cautionary announcement on Wednesday by BOE Natwest Ltd saying it was in talks with Real Afrika Durolink (Pty) Ltd which could affect the share prices of Boland, Samgro and NBS as well as those of Board of Executors Ltd, BOE Corp Ltd and Pepgro Ltd.
